findings.criterion: A defect-seeded duplicate prerequisite build fails the deterministic call-count oracle, and a defect-seeded missing COMMIT still fails the provenance oracle.
findings.detail: The test file tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py contains no call-count oracle, no subprocess seam, and no deterministic build-call counting mechanism. The ticket plan (step 5) required strengthening the module with "deterministic build-call counting under a subprocess seam or equivalent fixture-level contract" so that a defect-seeded duplicate build would fail a counter oracle. No such oracle or counter exists in the committed file. The ticket comment mentions a "held-out oracle /tmp/rebar_build_count_oracle.py" — this is an external file not committed to the repository. Searching for 'oracle', 'call_count', 'count', 'defect' in the test file confirms none of these mechanisms are present. The provenance assertion (test_wheel_from_sdist_bakes_env_commit) does implicitly cover the COMMIT check, but there is no explicit defect-seeded test case for a missing COMMIT, and no call-count oracle at all.
findings.remediation: Add a deterministic call-count oracle to tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py — either a subprocess seam that counts how many times `python -m build` is invoked with REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT=abc1234, or an equivalent fixture-level counter — and add a test that asserts exactly 1 successful prerequisite build per session. Also add a defect-seeded test that corrupts the shared wheel's COMMIT and verifies the provenance assertion returns RED.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
